documents.title: chest cold
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Been coughing up green stuff for 2 days and more short of breath than usual. No fever. Can I come in today

documents.title: RE: chest cold
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Yes - PCP can see you at 11:15 today. If your breathing gets much worse before then, call 911.

medications.sig: Take 2 tablets (40 mg) by mouth once daily with breakfast for 5 days
Take 1 capsule by mouth twice daily for 7 days; take with water and stay upright 30 minutes

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Rooming Note
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Roomed. Vitals taken. Med list reviewed with pt - no changes, no new outside meds. Tobacco: current, 1 ppd. Pt declines quitline info today.

documents.title: Same-Day Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Same-day sick visit (portal message this AM).

S: Five days of worse cough. Sputum turned thick yellow-green two days ago, more of it. More winded than his usual - stops walking across the kitchen. Wheezy at night. No fever at home, mild chills one night. No chest pain beyond soreness from coughing. No leg swelling. Using olodaterol daily since this started.
Smoking: cut down to a few cigarettes a day since he got sick.

O: T 36.7, HR 73, RR 14, BP 149/92, SpO2 89% RA.
Talking in full sentences. Lungs: diffuse expiratory wheeze and coarse rhonchi, clearing partly with cough; no focal crackles, no dullness. Prolonged expiration. Heart regular. No edema.

A/P
Acute bronchitis in a man with severe COPD, purulent sputum.
- Prednisone 40 mg daily x 5 days.
- Doxycycline 100 mg BID x 7 days for the purulent sputum.
- Olodaterol daily.
- No signs of pneumonia on exam; will image if fever or not improving.
- Call or go to ED for worse breathing, confusion, chest pain.
- Sugar/BP may run up on prednisone, short course.
- Smoking: good moment to stay cut down - encouraged.
Check in by portal in a week.

documents.title: checking in
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Finished the prednisone and almost done the antibiotic. Phlegm is back to white mostly and I'm breathing like normal for me. Thanks. Lyle

documents.title: RE: checking in
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad to hear it. Finish the doxycycline. Keep the olodaterol going every day - not just when you're sick. And let me know if the phlegm turns colored again.

documents.title: Triage call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called - wheezy and tight since Friday, more cough, sputum clear/white, no fever. Speaking full sentences on phone. Same-day slot 3 PM with PCP.

medications.sig: Take 2 tablets (40 mg) by mouth once daily with breakfast for 5 days

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Rooming Note
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pt roomed, vitals entered. Brought med bottles; reconciled, matches list. Smoking status updated (every day).

documents.title: Same-Day Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Same-day visit.

S: Chest cold since Friday - more cough, more wheeze, tight chest, more breathless than baseline. Sputum more of it but white/clear this time. No fever. No chest pain. Second one this winter (January, treated with prednisone + doxy).
Smoking: back to about a pack a day since February.

O: T 37.2, HR 76, RR 14, BP 153/96, SpO2 88% RA.
Lungs: expiratory wheeze throughout, prolonged expiration, no crackles. Heart regular. No edema.

A/P
Acute bronchitis on COPD, non-purulent.
- Prednisone 40 mg x 5 days.
- No antibiotic - sputum not purulent, afebrile.
- Olodaterol daily.
- Return/ED precautions reviewed.
- Two episodes in three months; he has pulm f/u in July - will make sure they know.
- Smoking: counseled, he knows.

documents.title: better
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Breathing back to my usual. Done with the pills.

documents.title: RE: better
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Thanks for letting us know, Mr. Haskins. PCP will see you at your May visit.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Rooming Note
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Rooming: vitals done, seated 5 min before BP. Meds verified verbally. Still smoking. No falls since last visit.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u after two bronchitis episodes (1/27, 4/8).

Back to baseline breathing, which is poor - stairs, inclines. Chronic productive cough. Exertional chest tightness unchanged. Calves at two blocks.
Olodaterol 'most days.'
Smoking 1 ppd.

Vitals: BP 154/99, HR 66, SpO2 89% RA.
Exam: diminished BS, prolonged exp, few wheezes. Heart regular. No edema.

A/P
1. COPD with two bronchitis episodes this year - pulm f/u 7/16, message sent to them with the dates.
2. HTN/HHD - 154/99. Lisinopril, HCTZ, metoprolol unchanged.
3. AAA - vascular surgery scan due; pt has appt in June.
4. Tobacco - counseled.

RTC after pulm / AWV.

reports.text:
VASCULAR LABORATORY - ABDOMINAL AORTA ULTRASOUND
Indication: infrarenal AAA surveillance.
Comparison: 06/06/2023, 4.4 cm.
Fusiform infrarenal AAA, maximal outer-wall diameter 4.6 cm.
reports.conclusion: Infrarenal AAA 4.6 cm (4.4 cm in 2023). Below repair threshold.

documents.title: Vascular Surgery Surveillance Letter
documents.author: vascular surgery
documents.body:
VASCULAR SURGERY ASSOCIATES

Dear Doctor,

Mr. Haskins's aortic ultrasound on 06/17/2025 shows the infrarenal aneurysm at 4.6 cm, up from 4.4 cm two years ago. This is still below the size at which we would recommend repair, and he has no symptoms referable to it.

Given the slow growth, we will shorten his interval to a repeat ultrasound in 12 months. We again advised smoking cessation and reviewed warning symptoms.

Sincerely,
Vascular Surgery

Lungs are hyperinflated with flattened hemidiaphragms. No focal consolidation, effusion or pneumothorax.

Acceptable efforts.

documents.title: Pulmonology Follow-up
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
PULMONOLOGY CLINIC NOTE
Date of visit: 07/16/2025

71-year-old man with COPD and coronary disease after MI, seen for continued care of his respiratory symptoms; last here a year ago.

Breathing is worse again. Still coughing up sputum most mornings. For about two years he has been getting chest infections more often than he used to, and his PCP has treated him twice since January for bronchitis. He says he is tired of being short of breath and is open to making changes.
Smoking history about 45 pack-years per his report today.

SpO2 92% on room air.
Exam: prolonged expiratory phase with wheezing; reduced breath sounds at the bases.

Chest x-ray: hyperinflation and flattened diaphragms.
Spirometry: FEV1/FVC 0.65, minimally reversible with bronchodilator.

Assessment: COPD with chronic productive cough and recurrent bronchitis; continued smoking.

Plan: Discussed smoking cessation at length; he is open to it for the first time. Follow up with primary care. Return to pulmonology in one year.

documents.title: Rooming Note
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Roomed for f/u. Med rec complete. Pt reports no ED visits or hospital stays since last visit. Tobacco use: yes, daily.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV subsequent.

Outside notes reviewed:
- Pulm 7/16: CXR hyperinflation, flattened diaphragms; spirometry FEV1/FVC 0.65, minimally reversible. Smoking cessation discussed; he told them he is willing to consider changes. Return 1 yr.
- Vascular surgery 6/17: AAA 4.6 cm (4.4 in 2023), below repair threshold, rescan 12 mo.
Two bronchitis episodes this year (Jan, Apr). None since.

He brought up quitting himself today - usually I'm the one raising it. Wants to think about a date around the holidays. Talked about what's worked for others; he'd like to try on his own first.

HRA: independent, no falls, uses railings. PHQ-2 1. Alcohol 1-2/wk.
Tobacco 1 ppd, ~51 pk-yr.

Vitals: BP 150/94, HR 66, SpO2 92% RA, wt 92.7.
Exam: barrel chest, diminished BS, prolonged exp. Heart regular. Abd soft, pulsatile mass. Pedal pulses diminished. No edema.

Prevention: LDCT ordered (last 10/2024 Lung-RADS 2). FIT kit. Flu/COVID October.

A/P
1. COPD - olodaterol. Recurrent bronchitis this year.
2. HTN/HHD - 150/94. Continue lisinopril, HCTZ, metoprolol.
3. CAD/HLD - labs today.
4. AAA 4.6 cm - vascular surgery 12 mo.
5. PAD - stable.
6. Tobacco - contemplating. Revisit at December visit.

RTC 3-4 mo.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text:
LOW-DOSE CT CHEST, LUNG CANCER SCREENING - ANNUAL
Comparison: 10/08/2024 and back to 08/11/2020.
Lungs: Centrilobular emphysema, upper lobe predominant. 4 mm right upper lobe solid nodule, stable for five years. No new nodule.
Pleura and mediastinum: unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 2. Emphysema. Annual screening in 12 months.
